stories.headline: 7.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Panama, tsunami threat issued for nine countries in Central and South America
stories.title: 7.7-magnitude earthquake strikes Panama, tsunami threat issued for nine countries in Central and South America
stories.summary: Panama, Oct 10 : An earthquake of magnitude 7.7 struck off Panama on Friday night. The US Embassy in Panama warned of possible aftershocks and potential tsunami threats across nine countries in Central and South America. In a post shared on X, the National Centre for Seismology (NCS) said the earthquake occurred at 11:26 pm IST on October 9 at a depth of 10 kilometres. According to the details shared, the epicentre was located 206 kilometres southwest of Panama City, Panama. Meanwhile, the US Embassy in Panama said a magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck in La Pitaloza, Panama, at 12:56 local time on October 9, with the location approximately 14 kilometres southwest of Pitaloza Arriba. The embassy warned that aftershocks capable of causing damage may occur. It also said the US Tsunami Warning System had issued potential tsunami threats for Costa Rica, El Salvador, Peru, Mexico, Guatemala, Panama, Nicaragua, Colombia and Ecuador. “Strong and unusual currents and unpredictable surges may occur along the shore,” the embassy said, advising US citizens in the affected areas to stay away from damaged structures and monitor local emergency broadcasts and official guidance for updates. The embassy urged people to avoid damaged areas and refrain from entering damaged buildings. It also advised those near the coast to move to higher ground and follow instructions issued by local authorities. It further warned people to be prepared for possible power and communication outages.

stories.title: Woman Moves Karnataka High Court Seeking LOC Against Husband In Dowry Case

article_sentences: A woman has approached the Karnataka High Court seeking a direction to the police to initiate the process for issuance of a Look Out Circular (LOC) against her husband, a France-based working professional accused of cruelty and dowry harassment.
The wife contends that her husband remains in India only pending reissuance of his allegedly lost passport and that his departure would prejudice the ongoing investigation.
Advocate Angad Kamath mentioned the matter yesterday before Justice Anant Ramananth Hegde.
The matter is likely to be taken up next week.

The plea challenges an October 8 order of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (CMM) Court rejecting her application under Section 175(3) read with Section 94 BNSS, seeking a direction to the Investigating Officer to request issuance of an LOC and intimate the Regional Passport Officer about the pending criminal case.
"A Look Out Circular opened on the direction sought can be deleted the day this Petition fails; the departure of Accused No. 1 cannot be undone by any order thereafter," the plea states.
The couple married in November 2022.
On September 30, the wife lodged a complaint alleging physical, mental and economic cruelty, unlawful demands for money and retention of her wedding gold.
An FIR was registered under Sections 85, 352 and 351(2) BNS and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
According to the plea, the husband ordinarily resides in France, where he has a valid residence permit, an indefinite-term employment contract and an apartment.
He arrived in India on August 23 and had a confirmed return flight for October 1, but did not board it.
He subsequently reported his passport lost.

stories.headline: When Can ECI Choose Not To Hold Bye-Election? Supreme Court Reserves Judgment On Interpretation Of S.151A RP Act
stories.title: When Can ECI Choose Not To Hold Bye-Election? Supreme Court Reserves Judgment On Interpretation Of S.151A RP Act
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court recently reserved judgment on the interpretation of Section 151A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, which prescribes a six-month period for holding bye-elections to fill casual vacancies in Parliament and State Legislatures, subject to certain exceptions.

A bench of Justice Vikram Nath, Justice Augustine George Masih and Justice Sandeep Mehta reserved the judgment in the Election Commission of India's plea challenging a December 2023 Bombay High Court judgment directing it to hold a bye-election for the Pune Lok Sabha constituency.

Section 151A provides that a bye-election to fill a casual vacancy "shall be held within a period of six months from the date of the occurrence of the vacancy." However, the proviso states that the provision will not apply if "the remainder of the term of a member in relation to a vacancy is less than one year." A further exception applies where the Election Commission, in consultation with the Central Government, certifies that it is difficult to hold the bye-election within the six-month period.
The question is from what point the one-year period under the first exception is to be calculated.
The Bombay High Court held that the relevant date is the date on which the vacancy occurs.
The Pune Lok Sabha seat fell vacant on March 29, 2023 while the term of the 17th Lok Sabha was due to expire over 14 months later on June 16, 2024.
The High Court held that the one-year exception in Section 151A did not apply a bye-election had to be conducted.
The ECI has contended that the six-month period available to the ECI for conducting the bye-election has to be accounted for while determining whether the one-year exception applies.
The issue arose from the vacancy in the Pune Lok Sabha constituency following the death of sitting MP Girish Bapat on March 29, 2023.
The term of the 17th Lok Sabha was due to end on June 16, 2024.
The ECI declined to hold a bye-election, issuing a certificate under Section 151A stating that it was difficult to conduct the election.

It cited, among other reasons, its engagement with elections and preparations for the 2024 Lok Sabha elections and the fact that the candidate elected in a bye-election would have only a limited period in office.

stories.headline: "I should have won 8 Nobel Peace Prizes": Trump slams Nobel Committee for awarding Navi Pillay
stories.title: "I should have won 8 Nobel Peace Prizes": Trump slams Nobel Committee for awarding Navi Pillay
stories.summary: Washington, October 10 : US President Donald Trump on Saturday criticised the Norwegian Nobel Committee for awarding the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize to Indian-origin South African jurist Navi Pillay, claiming that he deserved the honour for his role in resolving conflicts across the world. In a lengthy post on Truth Social on Friday (local time), Trump questioned Pillay's credentials and accused her of being opposed to Israel, while reiterating his claim that he had settled eight wars and deserved multiple Nobel Peace Prizes. “This is the woman who received the Nobel Peace Prize over the Great United States of America, whose Representative, ME, settled eight Wars, and many other things. I know nothing about this woman, and neither does anyone else!” Trump said. He added, “In fact, to the best of my knowledge, no one ever heard of her other than the fact that she, very obviously, hates Israel.” Trump listed eight conflicts that he claimed to have settled, including Cambodia and Thailand, Kosovo and Serbia, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda, Pakistan and India, Israel and Iran, Egypt and Ethiopia, Armenia and Azerbaijan, and Israel and Hamas. “I settled 8 Wars, with letters being sent from every President and Prime Minister from the countries that I helped to the Norwegian Nobel Committee, and I’m about to settle, or win, two more, Iran and, Russia/Ukraine,” he said. “Based on my record of PEACE, a record like no one else has ever achieved, I agree! I got back all of the hostages in Israel, including the final 28, both living and dead, and worked with Hamas to do it -- Nobody believed this was possible!” Trump added, while citing his other claimed achievements in international diplomacy and security. He further asserted that he had prevented Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon and claimed to have helped avert conflicts in other regions, including tensions involving North Korea, South Korea, Japan, China and Taiwan. “In actuality, I should have won 8 Nobel Peace Prizes, not just 1,” Trump said, referring to the conflicts he claimed to have resolved. The US President also criticised the United Nations, saying it had not helped in resolving the conflicts he cited. “In all of the Wars that I have settled, I never spoke to the United Nations--they were of no help,” he said. “The United States of America, represented by me, as your President, should have received the Nobel Peace Prize, but didn’t. This is an indelible stain on Norway, one that will never be forgotten,” Trump added. He further declared that the Nobel Peace Prize had been “forever discredited by a handful of Radical Ideologues who are Anti-Democracy, and Enemies of Civilization!” Trump's remarks came after Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif reiterated his support for the US President's Nobel Peace Prize bid. “In recognition of his outstanding contribution, Pakistan had nominated President Trump for the Nobel Peace Prize,” Sharif said, adding that he hoped Trump's efforts to promote peace would receive recognition. Meanwhile, the United States announced additional sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC) on Friday (local time), citing concerns over American sovereignty and the threat posed by the international judicial body. The announcement came on the same day the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Pillay. In a statement, the Norwegian Nobel Committee said Pillay had demonstrated exceptional courage and integrity in advancing a more comprehensive global legal order and had played a significant role in ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide were prosecuted. Pillay, a former United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, has served as a judge on South Africa's High Court, the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and the International Criminal Court. She also chaired the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory until recently and is currently a judge at the International Court of Justice in the case in which Myanmar stands accused of genocide. In response to the India-Pakistan ceasefire, New Delhi has consistently disputed Trump's claims while remaining steadfast in rejecting any external mediation. India has reiterated that the ceasefire understanding during Operation Sindoor was reached only after Pakistan's Director General of Military Operations (DGMO) reached out to his Indian counterpart to request a halt in military action. India had launched Operation Sindoor on May 7 last year as a decisive, targeted response to destroy terror infrastructure across Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK). The anti-terror operation was carried out to dismantle terror bases that were utilised to plan the horrific April 22 terrorist attack in Pahalgam. Following effective Indian strikes that dismantled key terror launchpads, the operation was paused on May 10 after a formal request from the Pakistani side. (ANI)

stories.headline: Kashmir slipping into darkness!
stories.title: Kashmir slipping into darkness!
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir is known as the “Paradise on Earth” by virtue of its astonishing natural landscapes, snow-capped mountains, crystal-clear lakes, and vibrant changing seasons. The region is endowed with massive mountain ranges like the Himalayas and Pir Panjal, deep green valleys, meadows, and pristine water bodies & rivers like Dal Lake, Wular, and Jhelum. Spring brings blooming tulip gardens, yellow mustard fields and pink almond flowers around karewas of Pulwama and Budgam. The summer offers lush greenery, gushing waters in streams , the autumn turns the trees into vibrant gold and red hues, and winter turns the region into a snowy wonderland. Sadly the current situation - “surat e haal” - does not offer a rosy picture of Kashmir. As per the recent National Clean Air Survey (Swachh Vayu Survekshan) Srinagar has been ranked at 26th place among 39 Indian cities with a population of 10 lakh or more. In the first survey that was launched in 2023 Srinagar ranked 4th. What has happened in last 3 years that Srinagar came down 22 steps downwards ? Burning of MSW The municipal solid waste is being burnt openly by sanitation staff across J&K and even Srinagar. Dust control mechanism is not in place. There has been a mushroom growth of vehicles emitting vehicular emission and causing heavy damage to ambient air quality. Illegal cement plants and stone crushers have are running openly without appropriate checks. No suitable measures have been taken for construction and demolition waste management system. There is lack of public awareness regarding air pollution by authorities and all these things contribute for air pollution in Srinagar and other districts of J&K. Last year the Air Quality Index -AQI touched almost 300 and this autumn and early winter would be terrible. Govt has to act and MLAs must put pressure on authorities during the ongoing session of assembly ? It is a matter of concern that Srinagar is behind Delhi vis a vis air quality. Delhi has for long made headlines with toxic winter smog and features among India’s most persistent air-pollution. Delhi secured the 21st rank with 172 points and Srinagar scored 162.6 points with 26th rank. According to the survey Lucknow ranks number one followed by Indore, Jabalpur, and Bhopal. The Swachh Vayu Survekshan Clean Air Survey was initiated in 2023 by the Government of India Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) under its National Clean Air Programme-NCAP and the survey is conducted by the Central Pollution Control Board-CPCB New Delhi. Although more than half of 130 non-attainment cities spent less than 50 per cent of the funds released under NCAP and 15th Finance Commission grants, Jammu and Kashmir offers a unsettling scene regarding utilisation of funds received under NCAP. Jammu & Kashmir received Rs 21 Crores between 2019 to June 2022 under NCPA crore but only Rs 12 lakh was spent constituting merely 0.5 per cent ? If less than 1 % of the funds were spent over three years soon since NCAP was launched, programme execution and implementation raises questions regarding accountability. When we compare this with states like Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh or Himachal they have spent good amount of money. In the same period Gujarat got Rs 12 crore and spent 100 per cent of the funds. Andhra Pradesh received Rs 34 crore and spent Rs 22 crore, while Himachal Pradesh received Rs 10 crore and spent Rs 6.30 crore as per the information provided by Ministry of Environment Forest and Climate Change. CAG Report As far as environmental degradation vis a vis waterbodies and lakes of Jammu & Kashmir are concerned, the story is not different. The recent CAG report has disclosed that more than 500 lakes in Jammu and Kashmir have either vanished or significantly receded due to encroachments, siltation, and untreated sewage inflow, weakening natural flood buffers. Of the total lakes, 315 (45 %) covering 1,537.07 hectares have completely disappeared from official records. These include 80 lakes under the jurisdiction of the Forest / Wildlife Department and 235 under the Revenue and Agriculture departments. The report warned that the disappearance and shrinkage of 518 lakes have led to ecosystem degradation, loss of water resources, food and biodiversity, and disruption of carbon, nutrient, and water cycles, heightening climate vulnerability in the region. The primary reasons for the disappearance and shrinkage of lakes were identified as land-use changes within lakes and their catchment areas. Other contributing factors include deforestation, climate change, and altered catchment dynamics. The CAG audit also underlined deficiencies in conservation and management practices. According to the report, government conservation efforts were limited to only six lakes—Dal, Wular, Hokersar, Manasbal, Surinsar, and Mansar—which were examined in detail. For the remaining 691 lakes, the Forest Department neither identified eligible water bodies nor formulated plans to seek assistance under schemes of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC). The audit also flagged several issues affecting Dal Lake, including land-use changes due to non-acquisition of land from dwellers, malfunctioning sewage treatment plants (STPs), ineffective de-weeding mechanisms, and inadequate monitoring and surveillance. The CAG has recommended the establishment of a centralised and specialised authority equipped with adequate resources to ensure coordinated, accountable, and effective lake conservation and management. It also called for the deployment of skilled manpower, including environmental and hydrological engineers, wetland ecologists, limnologists, remote sensing and GIS specialists. SC, NGT intervention Fresh cloudbursts in the Pir Panjal & Chenab Valley, the rapid melting of the Amarnath ice lingam, mountains of untreated waste and relentless riverbed mining are jaw-dropper crises. Even Supreme Court has expressed concern over illegal mining in Shaliganga stream in the case of Govt of J&K & others v/s Raja Muzaffar Bhat Civil Appeal No. 8055 of 2022. After the Apex Courts Judgement dated August 22nd 2025 the J&K Pollution Control Committee -JKPCC has imposed Environmental Compensation of Rs 3.10 crore on a construction company NKC Projects Pvt Ltd in Feb 2026. This amount had to be paid in 3 months and now with the lapse of 6 months , the penalty amount has surged 3 times. The company has to pay Rs 12.30 crore and JKPCC has now asked the National Highway Authority of India -NHAI to retrieve the compensation money from pending bills of the company. This information was revealed on the floor of J&K Assembly few days back by J&K’s Mining Minister in response to MLA of Chadoora assembly segment in Budgam district. The last year’s cloudburst in Chisoti village in Kishtwar district claiming more than 75 people is still fresh in the minds of the people of Jammu and Kashmir. Another cloudburst had now struck the region, triggering flash floods and mudslides that damaged roads in Doda, Kishtwar and Ramban. Transport along the Jammu-Doda-Kishtwar highway came to a halt. Illegal mining of sand, gravel and boulders has intensified in recent years, damaging streams from Kathua to Kupwara and Budgam to Baramulla. In addition to it illegal earth mining in the Karewas of Budgam , Pulwama, Baramulla , Anantnag has caused devastation in these areas and NGT has taken cognizance of this case as well. The JKPCCs report submitted in NGT few months back revealed that 18 lakh Metric Tons clay, sand and gravel were excavated from just two villages of Gowherpora and Zadoora alone in Budgam and Pulwama districts. Although legal action through the National Green Tribunal has curbed machine-based extraction in rivers such as Doodh Ganga, Shaliganga and Sukhnag, manual extraction continues and cumulative damage has transformed river channels. Conclusion Jammu and Kashmir has reached the point where piecemeal responses no longer match the scale of the challenge. Climate adaptation must guide infrastructure planning, pilgrimage management, mining enforcement, waste processing, groundwater protection and disaster preparedness through one coordinated strategy backed by measurable goals and public accountability. Government declarations alone solve little. Public recognition changes priorities, mobilizes resources and signals that environmental protection sits alongside economic development instead of behind it. Jammu and Kashmir now faces a choice between continued crisis management and a comprehensive climate response. K P Yadaw is former Principal Accountant General J&K who was posted in J&K just before his retirement in Oct 2025 Raja Muzaffar Bhat is Founder of J&K RTI Movement , Chairman of J&K Climate Action Group

The Swachh Vayu Survekshan Clean Air Survey was initiated in 2023 by the Government of India Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) under its National Clean Air Programme-NCAP and the survey is conducted by the Central Pollution Control Board-CPCB New Delhi.

Although more than half of 130 non-attainment cities spent less than 50 per cent of the funds released under NCAP and 15th Finance Commission grants, Jammu and Kashmir offers a unsettling scene regarding utilisation of funds received under NCAP.
Jammu & Kashmir received Rs 21 Crores between 2019 to June 2022 under NCPA crore but only Rs 12 lakh was spent constituting merely 0.5 per cent?
If less than 1 % of the funds were spent over three years soon since NCAP was launched, programme execution and implementation raises questions regarding accountability.
When we compare this with states like Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh or Himachal they have spent good amount of money.
In the same period Gujarat got Rs 12 crore and spent 100 per cent of the funds.

Andhra Pradesh received Rs 34 crore and spent Rs 22 crore, while Himachal Pradesh received Rs 10 crore and spent Rs 6.30 crore as per the information provided by Ministry of Environment Forest and Climate Change.
CAG Report As far as environmental degradation vis a vis waterbodies and lakes of Jammu & Kashmir are concerned, the story is not different.

The recent CAG report has disclosed that more than 500 lakes in Jammu and Kashmir have either vanished or significantly receded due to encroachments, siltation, and untreated sewage inflow, weakening natural flood buffers.
Of the total lakes, 315 (45 %) covering 1,537.07 hectares have completely disappeared from official records.
These include 80 lakes under the jurisdiction of the Forest / Wildlife Department and 235 under the Revenue and Agriculture departments.

The report warned that the disappearance and shrinkage of 518 lakes have led to ecosystem degradation, loss of water resources, food and biodiversity, and disruption of carbon, nutrient, and water cycles, heightening climate vulnerability in the region.
The primary reasons for the disappearance and shrinkage of lakes were identified as land-use changes within lakes and their catchment areas.
Other contributing factors include deforestation, climate change, and altered catchment dynamics.
The CAG audit also underlined deficiencies in conservation and management practices.
According to the report, government conservation efforts were limited to only six lakes—Dal, Wular, Hokersar, Manasbal, Surinsar, and Mansar—which were examined in detail.

For the remaining 691 lakes, the Forest Department neither identified eligible water bodies nor formulated plans to seek assistance under schemes of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC).

The audit also flagged several issues affecting Dal Lake, including land-use changes due to non-acquisition of land from dwellers, malfunctioning sewage treatment plants (STPs), ineffective de-weeding mechanisms, and inadequate monitoring and surveillance.

The CAG has recommended the establishment of a centralised and specialised authority equipped with adequate resources to ensure coordinated, accountable, and effective lake conservation and management.
It also called for the deployment of skilled manpower, including environmental and hydrological engineers, wetland ecologists, limnologists, remote sensing and GIS specialists.

SC, NGT intervention Fresh cloudbursts in the Pir Panjal & Chenab Valley, the rapid melting of the Amarnath ice lingam, mountains of untreated waste and relentless riverbed mining are jaw-dropper crises.
Even Supreme Court has expressed concern over illegal mining in Shaliganga stream in the case of Govt of J&K & others v/s Raja Muzaffar Bhat Civil Appeal No. 8055 of 2022.

After the Apex Courts Judgement dated August 22nd 2025 the J&K Pollution Control Committee -JKPCC has imposed Environmental Compensation of Rs 3.10 crore on a construction company NKC Projects Pvt Ltd in Feb 2026.
This amount had to be paid in 3 months and now with the lapse of 6 months, the penalty amount has surged 3 times.
The company has to pay Rs 12.30 crore and JKPCC has now asked the National Highway Authority of India -NHAI to retrieve the compensation money from pending bills of the company.
This information was revealed on the floor of J&K Assembly few days back by J&K’s Mining Minister in response to MLA of Chadoora assembly segment in Budgam district.
The last year’s cloudburst in Chisoti village in Kishtwar district claiming more than 75 people is still fresh in the minds of the people of Jammu and Kashmir.
Another cloudburst had now struck the region, triggering flash floods and mudslides that damaged roads in Doda, Kishtwar and Ramban.
Transport along the Jammu-Doda-Kishtwar highway came to a halt.
Illegal mining of sand, gravel and boulders has intensified in recent years, damaging streams from Kathua to Kupwara and Budgam to Baramulla.
In addition to it illegal earth mining in the Karewas of Budgam, Pulwama, Baramulla, Anantnag has caused devastation in these areas and NGT has taken cognizance of this case as well.

The JKPCCs report submitted in NGT few months back revealed that 18 lakh Metric Tons clay, sand and gravel were excavated from just two villages of Gowherpora and Zadoora alone in Budgam and Pulwama districts.

Although legal action through the National Green Tribunal has curbed machine-based extraction in rivers such as Doodh Ganga, Shaliganga and Sukhnag, manual extraction continues and cumulative damage has transformed river channels.
Conclusion Jammu and Kashmir has reached the point where piecemeal responses no longer match the scale of the challenge.

Climate adaptation must guide infrastructure planning, pilgrimage management, mining enforcement, waste processing, groundwater protection and disaster preparedness through one coordinated strategy backed by measurable goals and public accountability.
Government declarations alone solve little.
Public recognition changes priorities, mobilizes resources and signals that environmental protection sits alongside economic development instead of behind it.
Jammu and Kashmir now faces a choice between continued crisis management and a comprehensive climate response.

Motilal Oswal said concerns over a partial shift in telecom allocations from Bharti to Jio were “overblown” because Jio would initially have limited free float compared with Bharti’s foreign and domestic institutional ownership.
The brokerage also expects a smartphone tariff increase of about 15% in December 2026, following the Jio IPO and Vodafone Idea Ltd.’s planned fundraise.

stories.title: Nifty bulls regain momentum, but can bears strike back? 5 factors to decide D-Street’s fate next week
stories.summary: Indian equities staged a sharp rebound on Friday, October 9, bringing an end to the Nifty 50 and Sensex’s eight-week losing streak, with buying across information technology (IT), FMCG, auto and financial stocks lifting benchmark indices.The Nifty 50 gained 288.65 points, or 1.30%, to close at 22,520.45, while the Sensex advanced 879.09 points, or 1.23%, to settle at 72,472.33.However, the rebound comes against a challenging macroeconomic backdrop, with crude oil prices above $100 a barrel, sustained foreign investor outflows, a weaker rupee and tighter monetary policy continuing to weigh on sentiment. With domestic and US inflation data, global bond yields and more corporate earnings in focus, investors will assess whether Friday’s recovery can extend into the coming week.Also read: RBI tightens forex derivative rules: What changes for hedging, cancelled trades Can Nifty bulls sustain the recovery?Analysts remain cautious about the sustainability of the rebound, citing elevated crude prices, foreign investor selling and global macroeconomic uncertainty as key risks. While domestic institutional buying has cushioned the impact of overseas outflows and IT stocks have led Friday’s recovery, the next move will depend on inflation data, global bond yields, oil prices and the September-quarter earnings outlook.Here are the 5 factors that could decide D-Street’s fate next week:1. Crude oil prices and geopolitical tensionsCrude oil prices remain a key macroeconomic concern for Indian equities, with Brent crude trading above the $100-a-barrel mark and West Texas Intermediate (WTI) above $90. Uncertainty surrounding Iran, the Strait of Hormuz and regional energy infrastructure continues to raise concerns over potential supply disruptions, with implications for inflation, the import bill and the rupee."A renewed rise in crude could intensify inflationary pressure, weaken the rupee further and weigh on sectors sensitive to fuel and input costs," said Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money. He noted that a sustained decline in prices would offer meaningful relief to Indian equities by easing concerns over inflation and the country's import bill.Ponmudi added that diplomatic efforts had offered some hope of de-escalation, although the risk of further interruptions to energy shipments remained.Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, CEO of HST Wealth, also flagged elevated oil prices as a risk to the market outlook. He said Brent crude had settled above the $100 mark after trading in a range of roughly $102.50-$105, adding that a sustained decline below $100 would be needed to provide meaningful macroeconomic relief.ALSO READ: Wall Street Week Ahead: Bank earnings, CPI headline busy markets week as S&P 500 hovers near records2. US inflation, bond yields and the rupeeUS inflation and retail-sales data will be important triggers for global markets next week, as stronger readings could keep Treasury yields and the dollar elevated. In India, September consumer price inflation (CPI) and wholesale price inflation (WPI) data, analysts said, will offer cues on domestic price pressures and the potential implications for monetary policy.A stronger-than-expected CPI reading, Hariselvan said, could revive concerns over further Reserve Bank of India (RBI) tightening, putting rate-sensitive sectors such as banking, automobiles and real estate under pressure while raising the risk of a broader drag on consumer demand. A softer reading could ease concerns over the eventual peak in interest rates, although relief may prove short-lived if crude prices remain elevated. WPI inflation will provide further indications of how energy and logistics costs are filtering through to producer prices."Global bond yields will remain central to the direction of foreign flows," Ponmudi said. He noted that the US 10-year Treasury yield had eased from its recent peak near 5.36% to around 5.24%, providing some respite for emerging-market assets, although yields remained elevated."Any renewed rise in US yields could strengthen the dollar, increase pressure on the rupee and dampen risk appetite, particularly in rate-sensitive and higher-valued stocks," he said.Hariselvan, meanwhile, said US inflation and retail-sales data would influence the direction of Treasury yields and the dollar. "Stronger-than-expected readings could reinforce expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening, sustaining pressure on emerging-market currencies and foreign portfolio flows," he said. Conversely, softer inflation or signs of moderating consumer demand could pull yields lower and provide Indian equities with a firmer foundation for recovery.The rupee, trading near the Rs 97-per-dollar region, remains vulnerable to high crude prices, elevated US yields and sustained foreign portfolio outflows, according to Ponmudi. He added that a more durable recovery in the currency would likely require greater stability in oil prices and global yields, alongside an improvement in foreign investor flows.The RBI’s policy stance will also remain in focus. Ponmudi noted that the central bank’s October 7 decision to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% and shift its stance from neutral to calibrated tightening marked its first rate increase in nearly four years.The move reflected heightened concerns over inflation risks from elevated energy and commodity prices amid global uncertainty. Investors are likely to assess the implications for future policy decisions, borrowing costs and liquidity, with higher interest rates potentially weighing on credit-sensitive sectors and corporate financing conditions.3. FII flows versus domestic institutional buyingForeign investor selling remains a major overhang for the market, although domestic institutional investors have continued to absorb much of the selling pressure. FIIs recorded net outflows of approximately Rs 39,779 crore in October so far, while DIIs bought around Rs 40,355 crore over the same period, broadly offsetting the foreign selling.Hariselvan said domestic institutional investors had provided a crucial counterweight to foreign selling, absorbing nearly the entire Rs 30,000-crore weekly outflow from foreign institutional investors.The ability of domestic institutions to sustain this support, alongside any improvement in overseas investor flows, will remain important for the market’s direction. Ponmudi noted that elevated US bond yields could continue to limit overseas allocations to Indian equities, while a renewed rise in yields could strengthen the dollar and put further pressure on the rupee.4. IT earnings and sectoral momentumIT stocks led Friday’s recovery after TCS reported its September-quarter results, helping lift the broader indices. The focus now shifts to HCL Technologies, Wipro and Tech Mahindra, whose results and management commentary could determine whether the sector’s rebound gains traction.Ponmudi said corporate earnings would increasingly influence sector-level performance as the September-quarter results season gathers pace. Investors will look for evidence of earnings resilience, demand recovery and margin stability across sectors."Strong results and positive management commentary could encourage selective buying," Ponmudi said, adding that the sustainability of the recovery would depend on whether earnings strength could offset higher input costs, currency volatility and tighter monetary conditions.Hariselvan said the IT sector’s recovery would depend on the performance of its peers and their outlook for the coming quarters. "Management commentary on U.S. discretionary spending, deal conversions and margins will be key," he said.He also flagged the potential implications of the PERM suspension for Indian IT companies. While the restriction does not affect existing H-1B employment, a prolonged freeze could increase localisation and employee-retention costs, he said.5. Technical viewThe Nifty 50 staged a sharp recovery on Friday, ending its eight-week losing streak. However, the broader technical structure remains vulnerable as the index continues to trade below its key moving averages, warranting caution against interpreting the rebound as a confirmed trend reversal.The immediate resistance zone for the Nifty 50, according to Ponmudi, is placed around 22,600, followed by 22,800. A sustained move above 22,800 could strengthen the recovery and open the way towards 23,000. The index would need to reclaim and sustain above 23,000 to signal a more meaningful improvement in its short-term technical structure.On the downside, Ponmudi identified 22,400 as the immediate support zone, followed by 22,200 and the psychological 22,000 mark. A break below 22,200 could revive selling pressure and expose the index to lower levels.He noted that momentum indicators had improved from oversold territory following Friday’s rebound. stories.headline: Mediation must be preferred choice, not last resort: J&K HC judge
stories.title: Mediation must be preferred choice, not last resort: J&K HC judge
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 9: Mediation should be the preferred choice for dispute resolution rather than a last resort, Justice Rajnesh Oswal, Chairman of the Mediation and Conciliation Committee of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, said as a 40-hour role-play training programme for advocates and experts concluded at the J&K Judicial Academy campuses in Srinagar and Jammu on Friday. Justice Oswal encouraged participants to apply their newly acquired skills in practice and contribute to the Mediation for the Nation 3.0 initiative, emphasising the role of mediation in facilitating amicable settlements and helping parties move forward without bitterness. He said the spirit of mediation was inherent in everyday life, from families and schools to communities and professional relationships. Drawing on his judicial experience, he explained how mediation could help resolve even long-pending disputes where a settlement initially appeared unlikely. The training programme was organised under the aegis of the Mediation and Conciliation Project Committee (MCPC) of the Supreme Court of India by the Mediation and Conciliation Committee of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, in collaboration with the J&K Judicial Academy. The practical sessions were held on October 5, 6, 8 and 9. During the second day of the Srinagar session, Chief Justice of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, Dr Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati, highlighted the importance of mediation in strengthening the justice delivery system. He said mediation was not merely a professional skill but also a means of becoming a better human being and a more effective advocate, public prosecutor or judge. He emphasised that practical exercises and role-play sessions helped develop empathy, understanding and sensitivity in resolving disputes. Referring to Indian epics, religious traditions and Kashmir's history, the Chief Justice highlighted the longstanding cultural significance of peaceful dispute resolution. He also referred to Surah An-Nisa of the Holy Quran, observing that its provisions envisage a process resembling modern mediation, with representatives from both sides appointed to help restore harmony. Justice Bhati said examples across religious and cultural traditions demonstrated the enduring relevance of reconciliation and amicable settlement. Rajeev Gupta, in-charge Director of the J&K Judicial Academy, welcomed the dignitaries, resource persons and participants, stressing the importance of practical training in developing effective mediation skills. He said interactive exercises and simulated proceedings provided hands-on experience in facilitating amicable settlements. At the Srinagar campus, resource persons Monika Jalota and Swarn Sandhir, experienced advocates and certified mediators, conducted interactive sessions and role-play exercises to familiarise participants with mediation techniques and their practical application. The sessions were coordinated by Faizan-ul-Haq Iqbal, Coordinator, Main Mediation Centre. At the Jammu campus, Sunil Kumar, Secretary of the J&K Legal Services Committee, delivered the welcome address and stressed the need for practical training to develop competent mediators. The role-play sessions were conducted by Yashpal Singh Dahiya and Balbir Kaur Gandhi, resource persons associated with the MCPC. During the concluding session in Srinagar, Justice Oswal urged participants to use their skills to strengthen mediation as an effective mechanism for dispute resolution. Faizan-ul-Haq Iqbal proposed the vote of thanks, expressing gratitude to the Supreme Court of India, the MCPC, the High Court's Mediation and Conciliation Committee, the Judicial Academy's director and staff, and the resource persons for their support. The programme saw advocates and experts participate in simulated mediation proceedings designed to strengthen communication, negotiation and dispute-resolution skills. The initiative is part of ongoing efforts to expand the pool of trained mediators, promote timely and sustainable settlements, improve access to justice and reduce the burden of litigation.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Asks High Court To Re-Hear Plea Against Goa Female Weightlifter's Selection As Coach
stories.title: Supreme Court Asks High Court To Re-Hear Plea Against Goa Female Weightlifter's Selection As Coach
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court recently set aside the Bombay High Court's order, which disallowed Goa weightlifter Vaishnavi S. Ugadekar from selection to the post of Coach (Grade-IV) in Weightlifting.

A bench comprising Justice Prashant Kumar Mishra and Justice Shree Chandrashekhar observed that the High Court decision dismissed the plea without impleading or hearing her, despite her being one of only two candidates competing for the post.
This arose during the selection process where Ugadekar had raised a complaint regarding the fairness of the selection, following which the State Government directed that the tests be re-conducted.
The other candidate filed a writ petition challenging the decision before the High Court, which passed the impugned order without making Ugadekar a party.
The Court has now set aside this order and restored the writ petition for fresh consideration on merits, directing that Ugadekar be impleaded and both candidates be heard.
The Court also directed that its interim order shall continue during the pendency of the writ petition and requested the High Court to decide the matter at the earliest.

It noted: "Considering that the appellant and respondent No. 4 are the only two candidates competing for the post, we deem it appropriate to direct the High Court to decide the matter afresh after affording an opportunity of hearing to both parties.

Consequently, the impugned order is set aside, and the Writ Petition preferred by respondent No. 4 is restored to its original number for a decision afresh on merits upon hearing all parties to the Writ Petition, including the present appellant who shall be impleaded as a party before the High Court."
Further, it has directed that the High Court should decide the matter at the earliest.
The bench has however, clarified that the High Court shall decide the matter afresh on its own merits, uninfluenced by either its earlier order or the Supreme Court's order.
